item.title: What Happened in the War in the Middle East on Wednesday.
item.summary: Formidable strikes rocked Tehran early Wednesday morning. Iran launched what its state-aligned media called one of the largest attacks on Israel yet, damaging several cities.

item.title: In Speech, Trump Is Expected to Call Iran War a Success
Trump Laid Out Five Goals for the Iran War. Here’s Where They Stand.
item.summary: The United States and Israel have done significant damage to Iran’s military capabilities. But Iran still fires missiles, has nuclear material and coordinates with militias in the region.

item.title: Iran Is Skeptical About Diplomacy, U.S. Intelligence Says
item.summary: Any decision by Iran to keep fighting would complicate President Trump’s stated goal of trying to end the war within weeks.

item.title: Iran’s President Suggests Diplomatic Engagement Possible in Letter to U.S. Public
item.summary: The letter, by President Masoud Pezeshkian of Iran, was at times defiant, patronizing or conciliatory, and came hours before President Trump was set to address the American people on the war.

item.title: Evacuated From War-Torn Gaza, 11 Toddlers Return Home to Hugs and Tears
item.summary: The Palestinian children were born prematurely in the early days of the war and moved from a besieged hospital to Egypt. They have now returned home to the enclave, which lies in ruins.

item.title: Pentagon Is Doubling Fleet of A-10 Attack Planes in Middle East
item.summary: The slow-moving A-10 “Warthog” is a so-called close-air support plane that could be used to help U.S. ground forces seize territory near the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Heavy bombings across Tehran jolt its war-weary residents.
item.summary: Some people in the capital said the blasts on Wednesday morning were among the most powerful they had felt in more than a month of war.

item.title: Why Reopening the Strait of Hormuz Matters for the U.S. Economy
item.summary: The interconnectedness of global energy markets means that the effects of Iran’s blockade of the waterway are not limited to countries directly dependent on oil from the Middle East.

item.title: Placing U.S. Troops in Middle East Hotels May Violate Laws of War
item.summary: U.S. commanders have kept many troops away from bases in the region to protect them from Iran’s ballistic missile attacks.
